shared_elements: upright slab/monolith of grey weathered stone
carved (incised/low-relief) decoration on a single face
motifs stacked in vertical zones or registers
justification: Both are upright grey stone slabs whose single carved face is organised into stacked vertical zones, and both include a discrete ring/spiral disc motif among curvilinear band-work. The decisive difference is content and manner: A shows weathered, abstract low-relief symbols with no figures and no border, while B is a crisply framed panel with an interlace margin filled with two registers of silhouetted standing figures, presented as a flat illustration rather than a museum photograph.
